name: How to Compare Fencing Quotes That Handle Permits and Engineering Differently

mainEntity.name: How do I compare quotes from Los Angeles County fencing contractors when one includes permits and engineering and another does not?
mainEntity.text: How do I compare quotes from Los Angeles County fencing contractors when one includes permits and engineering and another does not?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fence estimates in Los Angeles County often look very different because some contractors bundle permits, engineering, and demolition, while others only price the basic fence. To compare fairly, ask every contractor to itemize the quote into clear categories: materials, labor, permit acquisition, engineering or structural calculations, old fence removal and haul-away, post-concrete depth, hardware, gates, and any retaining wall or grading work. If one bid includes permits and another expects you to handle them, request an approximate permit cost and expected time so you can factor that into the total. Do the same for engineering; complex or tall fences, pool barriers, and hillside projects can require professional calculations that significantly affect price. Clarify whether sales tax, dump fees, and potential access charges (tight yards, stair-only access, or alley work) are already included. Ask each contractor to list exclusions in writing—such as tree removal, roots, or underground utilities—to avoid surprise change orders once work starts. When you lay out all bids side by side with these line items, you can see whether a ‘cheaper’ quote is actually missing key services that you’ll have to pay for separately, helping you choose based on real overall value instead of just a low headline price.
acceptedAnswer.description: Break each fencing quote into materials, labor, permits, engineering, demolition, and extras like gates. Ask contractors to label what is included or excluded in writing so you can compare true total cost, not just the base fence price.
